To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a cytochrome-P450 monooxygenases that is involved in the detoxification of a broad spectrum of insecticides and developed an antibody-based lateral flow assay to detect this cytochrome P-450 in whiteflies, which can be used to monitor the spread of metabolic resistance.

we identified the first cytochrome P 450 monooxygenases conferring cross resistance to insecticides belonging to two unrelated chemical classes and developed a lateral flow assay to detect metabolic resistance mediated by CYP 6CM 1 in Bemisia.
we have developed a lateral flow test kit to detect metabolic resistance to insecticides mediated by the over expression of a cytochrome p450 enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in resistance to insecticides in B. tabaci, the development and validation of molecular diagnostic tests to detect resistance and the use of the test kit to support insecticide resistance management strategies.
the development of a lateral flow assay to detect metabolic resistance mediated by CYP 6CM1, in the whitefly Bemisia tabci.

the development of an easy to handle diagnostic tool for the identification of metabolic resistance in the cotton whitefly, B. tabaci, which will help farmers and extension workers to make more informed pest management decisions and reduce the risk of resistance evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CYP6CM2 is a major resistance gene in B. tabaci and that it confers resistance not only to imidaclopirid but also to other insecticides.

CYP6CMV1, a cyctochrome P450 enzyme, has been identified as the major factor contributing to the resistance of B. tabaci to neonicotind insecticides and that a lateral flow assay based diagnostic test has been developed to detect the presence of CYP6CMI protein in field collected B. tabaci populations.
CYP6CMV is a broad spectrum detoxifying enzyme, with a high level of catalytic versatility, and that it is the most important detoxification enzyme in Bemisia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a lateral flow test for the detection of metabolic resistance in B. tabaci mediated by the over expression of the cytochrome P 450 CYP6CM.
we developed the world’s first diagnostic lateral flow test to monitor metabolic insecticide resistance mediated by a single gene, CYP6CM.

we developed a lateral flow test kit to detect metabolic resistance mediated by CYP 6CM1, one of the most diverse insect detoxification enzymes yet discovered, and that this lateral flow test kit could be used in the field to support resistance management programs based on alternation of insecticides of differing modes of action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CYP6CMV1 is a major contributor to resistance to neonicitinoids and other insecticide classes in B. tabaci.
a lateral flow test can be developed to detect the over expression of a single detoxification enzyme, CYP6CMV1, in whitefly populations.
CYP6CM2 is one of the broadest spectrum detoxification enzymes yet discovered and that the lateral flow test can be used as an aid to support resistance management programs.
